question:
120 Year 10 students each chose one sport option. The two-way table shows some of the results.

| | Football | Netball | Swimming | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boys | 31 | | 18 | 56 |
| Girls | 15 | 33 | 16 | |
| Total | 46 | 40 | | 120 |

Complete the two-way table.
hint: Each row adds up to its row total and each column adds up to its column total. Each gap here can be found from one row or one column.
solution:
Use the fact that each row and each column must add up to its total.

Boys, Netball: $56 - 31 - 18 = 7$

Girls, Total: $15 + 33 + 16 = 64$

Total, Swimming: $120 - 46 - 40 = 34$

**Check:** the Swimming column gives $18 + 16 = 34$ and the Total column gives $56 + 64 = 120$.

| | Football | Netball | Swimming | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boys | 31 | 7 | 18 | 56 |
| Girls | 15 | 33 | 16 | 64 |
| Total | 46 | 40 | 34 | 120 |

This is the same survey of 120 Year 10 students, but different entries are missing this time.

| | Football | Netball | Swimming | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boys | 31 | | | 56 |
| Girls | | 33 | 16 | |
| Total | 46 | 40 | | 120 |

Complete the two-way table.
hint: Start with a row or column that has only one gap, e.g. the Football column. Some gaps can only be found after you have filled in others.
solution:
**What changed:** the gaps have moved. Now some rows and columns have two gaps, so you have to fill the cells in a sensible order.

Football column: girls $= 46 - 31 = 15$

Netball column: boys $= 40 - 33 = 7$

Boys row: swimming $= 56 - 31 - 7 = 18$

Girls row: total $= 15 + 33 + 16 = 64$

Swimming column: total $= 18 + 16 = 34$ (check: $120 - 46 - 40 = 34$ ✓)

| | Football | Netball | Swimming | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boys | 31 | 7 | 18 | 56 |
| Girls | 15 | 33 | 16 | 64 |
| Total | 46 | 40 | 34 | 120 |

question:
120 Year 10 students each chose one sport option: football, netball or swimming.

• 56 of the students are boys.
• 31 of the boys chose football.
• 46 students chose football.
• 33 girls chose netball.
• 40 students chose netball.
• 16 girls chose swimming.

Draw and complete a two-way table to show this information.
hint: Draw a table with rows Boys, Girls, Total and columns Football, Netball, Swimming, Total. Put each fact in its cell first, then fill the gaps.
solution:
**What changed:** the same data is now given in words, so the first job is to put each fact in the right cell.

Facts in the table: Boys total 56, Boys–Football 31, Football total 46, Girls–Netball 33, Netball total 40, Girls–Swimming 16, grand total 120.

Girls total $= 120 - 56 = 64$

Girls–Football $= 46 - 31 = 15$

Boys–Netball $= 40 - 33 = 7$

Boys–Swimming $= 56 - 31 - 7 = 18$

Swimming total $= 18 + 16 = 34$

| | Football | Netball | Swimming | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boys | 31 | 7 | 18 | 56 |
| Girls | 15 | 33 | 16 | 64 |
| Total | 46 | 40 | 34 | 120 |

question:
120 Year 10 students each chose one sport option: football, netball or swimming.

• $\frac{7}{15}$ of the students are boys.
• 31 of the boys chose football.
• 46 students chose football.
• 33 girls chose netball.
• 40 students chose netball.
• 16 girls chose swimming.

Draw and complete a two-way table to show this information.
hint: Work out $\frac{7}{15}$ of 120 to find the number of boys first.
solution:
**What changed:** one fact is now a fraction of the grand total instead of a count. Convert it first:
$$\frac{7}{15} \times 120 = 56 \text{ boys}$$

Now the information is the same as before:

Girls $= 120 - 56 = 64$; Girls–Football $= 46 - 31 = 15$; Boys–Netball $= 40 - 33 = 7$;
Boys–Swimming $= 56 - 31 - 7 = 18$; Swimming total $= 18 + 16 = 34$.

| | Football | Netball | Swimming | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boys | 31 | 7 | 18 | 56 |
| Girls | 15 | 33 | 16 | 64 |
| Total | 46 | 40 | 34 | 120 |

question:
200 adults were asked where they mainly get their news.

| | Online | TV | Newspaper | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Under 40 | 68 | 22 | 6 | 96 |
| 40 and over | 34 | 46 | 24 | 104 |
| Total | 102 | 68 | 30 | 200 |

Give each answer as a fraction in its simplest form and as a decimal to 3 decimal places where necessary.

Find

(a) the joint relative frequency of "under 40 and TV",

(b) the marginal relative frequency of "Newspaper",

(c) the proportion of the under-40s who mainly use online news,

(d) the proportion of the TV group who are aged 40 and over.
hint: Joint and marginal relative frequencies divide by the grand total, 200. For "the proportion of the under-40s…", divide by the under-40 total only.
solution:
(a) Joint: one cell $\div$ grand total.
$$\frac{22}{200} = \frac{11}{100} = 0.11$$

(b) Marginal: a column total $\div$ grand total.
$$\frac{30}{200} = \frac{3}{20} = 0.15$$

(c) Conditional: "of the under-40s" means divide by the under-40 total, 96.
$$\frac{68}{96} = \frac{17}{24} \approx 0.708$$

(d) Conditional: "of the TV group" means divide by the TV total, 68.
$$\frac{46}{68} = \frac{23}{34} \approx 0.676$$

Notice that (c) and (d) have different denominators: the phrase after "of the…" tells you which total to use.

question:
A survey of 150 households recorded where they live and whether they own a dog.

| | Dog | No dog | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Urban | 24 | 66 | 90 |
| Rural | 33 | 27 | 60 |
| Total | 57 | 93 | 150 |

The question asked: "What proportion of the dog owners live in a rural area?"

Priya's working is shown below.

Rural and dog $= 33$. There are 60 rural households.
Proportion $= \frac{33}{60} = 0.55$

(a) Identify Priya's error and explain why it is wrong.

(b) Work out the correct answer.

(c) Write a question for which $\frac{33}{60}$ **would** be the correct answer.
hint: The words "of the dog owners" tell you which group you are restricted to. What is the total of that group?
answer: (a) She divided by the rural total (60) instead of the dog-owner total (57). (b) $\frac{33}{57} = \frac{11}{19} \approx 0.579$ (c) "What proportion of rural households own a dog?"
solution:
(a) Priya used the wrong denominator. The condition is "of the **dog owners**", so we only look at the Dog column, whose total is 57. She divided by the Rural row total, 60, instead.

(b) Of the 57 dog owners, 33 live in a rural area:
$$\frac{33}{57} = \frac{11}{19} \approx 0.579$$

(c) $\frac{33}{60}$ is a proportion **of the rural households**: "What proportion of the rural households own a dog?" ($= 0.55$).

The two questions sound similar, but the condition changes the denominator.

question:
At a school, 150 Year 9 students and 90 Year 11 students were asked whether they read for pleasure every week. 45 of the Year 9 students and 36 of the Year 11 students said yes.

(a) Show this information in a two-way table.

(b) Tom says, "Year 9 students are more likely to read for pleasure than Year 11 students, because 45 is more than 36."

Is Tom correct? Justify your answer.
hint: The two year groups are different sizes. Compare the proportion of each year group who said yes.
answer: (a) Year 9: 45 yes, 105 no (150); Year 11: 36 yes, 54 no (90); totals 81, 159, 240. (b) No: $30\%$ of Year 9 but $40\%$ of Year 11 read for pleasure, so Year 11 students are more likely to.
solution:
(a)

| | Yes | No | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Year 9 | 45 | 105 | 150 |
| Year 11 | 36 | 54 | 90 |
| Total | 81 | 159 | 240 |

(b) Tom is **not** correct. He compared raw counts, but the groups are different sizes (150 and 90). Compare conditional proportions instead:

Year 9: $\frac{45}{150} = 0.3 = 30\%$

Year 11: $\frac{36}{90} = 0.4 = 40\%$

A greater proportion of Year 11 students read for pleasure, so Year 11 students are **more** likely to, even though fewer of them said yes.

question:
The segmented bar chart shows how students in Year 7 and Year 11 travel to school.

Leo writes:

The Bus segment for Year 7 goes up to $75\%$ and the Bus segment for Year 11 goes up to $70\%$.
So $75\%$ of Year 7 and $70\%$ of Year 11 travel by bus, which means a greater percentage of Year 7 travel by bus.

(a) Explain the mistake Leo has made.

(b) Find the correct percentages and write a correct conclusion.

(c) What percentage of Year 11 travel by car?
hint: The value of a segment is its length, not the height of its top edge. Where does each Bus segment start?
answer: (a) He read the top of each segment instead of its length. (b) Year 7: $30\%$, Year 11: $50\%$, so a greater percentage of Year 11 travel by bus. (c) $30\%$
solution:
(a) In a segmented bar chart each segment starts where the previous one ends. Leo has read the **top** of each Bus segment as its value, but the value is the **length** of the segment (top minus bottom).

(b) Year 7 Bus: from $45\%$ to $75\%$, so $75\% - 45\% = 30\%$.

Year 11 Bus: from $20\%$ to $70\%$, so $70\% - 20\% = 50\%$.

A greater percentage of **Year 11** students ($50\%$) travel by bus than Year 7 students ($30\%$). Leo's conclusion is reversed.

(c) Year 11 Car: from $70\%$ to $100\%$, so $100\% - 70\% = 30\%$.

question:
A car dealer recorded the fuel type of the new cars it sold in 2019 and in 2024.

| | Petrol | Hybrid | Electric | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 180 | 45 | 25 | 250 |
| 2024 | 96 | 84 | 60 | 240 |

The dealer has started a segmented bar chart. The bar for 2019 is complete.

(a) Show how the 2019 bar was worked out.

(b) Work out the percentages for 2024, and state the heights at which the boundaries between the segments of the 2024 bar should be drawn.

(c) The manager says, "We sold more petrol cars than electric cars in both years, so nothing has really changed." Use the chart to comment on whether there is an association between year and fuel type.
hint: Each bar shows percentages of that year's total. Stack the segments: the second boundary is the sum of the first two percentages.
answer: (a) $\frac{180}{250} = 72\%$, $\frac{45}{250} = 18\%$, $\frac{25}{250} = 10\%$; boundaries at $72\%$ and $90\%$. (b) Petrol $40\%$, Hybrid $35\%$, Electric $25\%$; boundaries at $40\%$ and $75\%$. (c) Yes, there is an association: the petrol share fell from $72\%$ to $40\%$ while hybrid rose from $18\%$ to $35\%$ and electric from $10\%$ to $25\%$.
solution:
(a) 2019 total = 250.

Petrol: $\frac{180}{250} \times 100 = 72\%$; Hybrid: $\frac{45}{250} \times 100 = 18\%$; Electric: $\frac{25}{250} \times 100 = 10\%$.

Stacking: Petrol from $0\%$ to $72\%$, Hybrid from $72\%$ to $72 + 18 = 90\%$, Electric from $90\%$ to $100\%$.

(b) 2024 total = 240.

Petrol: $\frac{96}{240} \times 100 = 40\%$; Hybrid: $\frac{84}{240} \times 100 = 35\%$; Electric: $\frac{60}{240} \times 100 = 25\%$.

Boundaries: $40\%$ (Petrol/Hybrid) and $40 + 35 = 75\%$ (Hybrid/Electric), with the bar ending at $100\%$.

(c) The manager is comparing counts within each year, which hides the change. Comparing the conditional percentages, the distribution of fuel type is very different in the two years: petrol fell from $72\%$ to $40\%$ of sales, hybrid nearly doubled from $18\%$ to $35\%$ and electric rose from $10\%$ to $25\%$. So there **is** an association between year and fuel type: a car sold in 2024 was much less likely to be petrol.

Using percentages also makes the comparison fair, because the dealer sold different numbers of cars in the two years (250 and 240).

question:
80 members of a gym were asked which session they usually attend: morning, afternoon or evening.

• 35 of the members are male.
• 12 of the males usually attend in the morning.
• 23 members usually attend in the afternoon. 9 of these are female.
• 18 of the females usually attend in the evening.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use this information to complete a two-way table.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
One of the 80 members is chosen at random.

Write down the probability that this member is female and usually attends in the evening.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt:
What fraction of the members who usually attend in the morning are female?

Give your answer in its simplest form.

hint: Start with the totals: how many females are there? Then use the afternoon column to find the afternoon males.
solution:
(a) Females $= 80 - 35 = 45$. Afternoon males $= 23 - 9 = 14$. Evening males $= 35 - 12 - 14 = 9$.
Morning females $= 45 - 9 - 18 = 18$.

| | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Male | 12 | 14 | 9 | 35 |
| Female | 18 | 9 | 18 | 45 |
| Total | 30 | 23 | 27 | 80 |

M1 for finding 45 females or 14 afternoon males; M1 for a correct method for at least two further entries; A1 for a fully correct table.

(b) $\frac{18}{80} = \frac{9}{40}$ B1 (accept unsimplified)

(c) Morning total $= 12 + 18 = 30$, of whom 18 are female.

$\frac{18}{30}$ M1 (denominator must be the morning total)

$= \frac{3}{5}$ A1

question:
The 40 members of a sports club each do either swimming or running.

| | Swimming | Running | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Junior | 8 | 12 | 20 |
| Senior | 5 | 15 | 20 |
| Total | 13 | 27 | 40 |

(a) A member is chosen at random. Given that the member does running, find the probability that the member is a junior.

(b) Two different members are chosen at random. Find the probability that both are juniors who do running.

(c) Two different members are chosen at random. Find the probability that exactly one of them does swimming.

Give your answers as fractions in their simplest form.
hint: For (a) restrict to the Running column. For (b) and (c) the second member is chosen from the 39 who are left, so the probabilities change; a tree diagram helps for (c).
solution:
(a) "Given that the member does running" restricts us to the Running column, total 27:
$$P(\text{junior} \mid \text{running}) = \frac{12}{27} = \frac{4}{9}$$

(b) There are 12 juniors who run. Choosing without replacement:
$$\frac{12}{40} \times \frac{11}{39} = \frac{132}{1560} = \frac{11}{130}$$

(c) 13 members swim and 27 run. Exactly one swimmer means (swim, run) or (run, swim):
$$\frac{13}{40} \times \frac{27}{39} + \frac{27}{40} \times \frac{13}{39} = 2 \times \frac{351}{1560} = \frac{702}{1560} = \frac{9}{20}$$

**Check:** $P(\text{both swim}) + P(\text{both run}) + P(\text{exactly one}) = \frac{156}{1560} + \frac{702}{1560} + \frac{702}{1560} = 1$ ✓

question:
150 people at a cinema were asked which type of film they prefer: comedy, action or animation. 70 of the people were children.

• 40 people chose comedy and 58 people chose action.
• $x$ adults and $y$ children chose comedy.
• Twice as many adults chose action as chose comedy.
• The number of children who chose action was the same as the number of children who chose comedy.

(a) Form two equations in $x$ and $y$ and solve them.

(b) Complete a two-way table for the survey.

(c) Show that the same number of adults as children chose animation.

(d) What proportion of the people who chose action were adults?
hint: Use the Comedy column total for one equation and the Action column total for the other.
solution:
(a) Comedy column: $x + y = 40$.

Adults choosing action $= 2x$; children choosing action $= y$. Action column: $2x + y = 58$.

Subtract the first equation from the second: $x = 18$. Then $y = 40 - 18 = 22$.

(b) Adults $= 150 - 70 = 80$. Adults: comedy 18, action $2 \times 18 = 36$, animation $80 - 18 - 36 = 26$.

Children: comedy 22, action 22, animation $70 - 22 - 22 = 26$.

| | Comedy | Action | Animation | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Adults | 18 | 36 | 26 | 80 |
| Children | 22 | 22 | 26 | 70 |
| Total | 40 | 58 | 52 | 150 |

(c) Adults choosing animation $= 26$ and children choosing animation $= 26$, so they are equal. (Check: animation total $= 150 - 40 - 58 = 52 = 26 + 26$ ✓)

(d) Restrict to the Action column, total 58: $\frac{36}{58} = \frac{18}{29} \approx 0.621$.

question:
A town council surveyed 400 residents about a proposed bypass.

• $55\%$ of the residents surveyed were aged under 50.
• $40\%$ of the residents aged under 50 supported the bypass.
• $65\%$ of the residents aged 50 and over supported the bypass.

(a) Construct a two-way table showing the numbers of residents.

(b) What percentage of the supporters were aged under 50? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

(c) A councillor says, "Only $42.9\%$ of under-50s support the bypass." Explain why the councillor is wrong.

(d) Is there an association between age group and support for the bypass? Give a reason.
hint: Find the number under 50 first ($55\%$ of 400). Each of the other percentages is a percentage of an age group, not of 400.
answer: (a) Under 50: 88 support, 132 against (220); 50 and over: 117 support, 63 against (180); totals 205, 195, 400 (b) $42.9\%$ (c) $42.9\%$ is the percentage of supporters who are under 50; the percentage of under-50s who support it is $40\%$. (d) Yes: $40\%$ of under-50s support it compared with $65\%$ of over-50s.
solution:
(a) Under 50: $0.55 \times 400 = 220$; 50 and over: $400 - 220 = 180$.

Under 50 supporting: $0.40 \times 220 = 88$; against: $220 - 88 = 132$.

50 and over supporting: $0.65 \times 180 = 117$; against: $180 - 117 = 63$.

| | Support | Against | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Under 50 | 88 | 132 | 220 |
| 50 and over | 117 | 63 | 180 |
| Total | 205 | 195 | 400 |

(b) Of the 205 supporters, 88 are under 50:
$$\frac{88}{205} \times 100 = 42.9\% \text{ (1 d.p.)}$$

(c) The councillor has confused the two conditional percentages. $42.9\%$ uses the supporters (205) as the denominator: it is the percentage **of supporters** who are under 50. The percentage **of under-50s** who support the bypass uses 220 as the denominator: $\frac{88}{220} = 40\%$.

(d) Yes. The conditional percentages supporting the bypass are $40\%$ for under-50s and $65\%$ for those aged 50 and over. These are clearly different, so support depends on age group: older residents were more likely to support it.

question:
A gardener grew 60 plants with fertiliser A and $k + 40$ plants with fertiliser B, and recorded whether each plant flowered.

| | Flowered | Did not flower | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fertiliser A | 36 | 24 | 60 |
| Fertiliser B | $k$ | 40 | $k + 40$ |

(a) Find the value of $k$ for which there is **no association** between fertiliser and flowering.

(b) For this value of $k$, show that the joint relative frequency of "fertiliser A and flowered" is equal to the product of the marginal relative frequencies of "fertiliser A" and "flowered".

(c) Explain what it would mean, in context, if $k$ were greater than your answer to (a).
hint: No association means the proportion that flowered is the same for both fertilisers.
answer: (a) $k = 60$ (b) $\frac{36}{160} = 0.225$ and $\frac{60}{160} \times \frac{96}{160} = 0.375 \times 0.6 = 0.225$ (c) A greater proportion of plants with fertiliser B would flower, so plants given B would be more likely to flower: there would be an association.
solution:
(a) No association means the conditional proportion that flowered is the same for each fertiliser.

Fertiliser A: $\frac{36}{60} = 0.6$.

Fertiliser B: $\frac{k}{k + 40} = 0.6 \Rightarrow k = 0.6k + 24 \Rightarrow 0.4k = 24 \Rightarrow k = 60$

(b) With $k = 60$: grand total $= 60 + 100 = 160$; flowered total $= 36 + 60 = 96$.

Joint relative frequency: $\frac{36}{160} = 0.225$

Product of marginals: $\frac{60}{160} \times \frac{96}{160} = 0.375 \times 0.6 = 0.225$ ✓

They are equal. This is what "no association" (independence) looks like: knowing the fertiliser does not change the chance of flowering.

(c) If $k > 60$, then $\frac{k}{k + 40} > 0.6$ (for example $k = 80$ gives $\frac{80}{120} \approx 0.67$). A greater proportion of fertiliser B plants would have flowered than fertiliser A plants, so there would be an association: plants given fertiliser B were more likely to flower. (This alone would not prove that B causes better flowering, unless the plants were randomly allocated to the fertilisers.)

question:
Two hospitals publish survival rates for the same operation. Each patient's condition before the operation was recorded as good or poor.

**Hospital A**

| | Survived | Died | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Good condition | 590 | 10 | 600 |
| Poor condition | 300 | 100 | 400 |

**Hospital B**

| | Survived | Died | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Good condition | 870 | 30 | 900 |
| Poor condition | 70 | 30 | 100 |

(a) Find the overall survival percentage for each hospital.

(b) Find the survival percentage for patients in good condition, and for patients in poor condition, at each hospital. Give your answers to 1 decimal place where necessary.

(c) A newspaper headline says "Hospital B is safer". Explain how your answers to (a) and (b) can both be true, and say which hospital you would choose for a patient in poor condition.
hint: In (c), look at what proportion of each hospital's patients were in poor condition.
answer: (a) A: $89\%$; B: $94\%$ (b) Good: A $98.3\%$, B $96.7\%$; Poor: A $75\%$, B $70\%$ (c) A has the higher survival rate in both groups, but B's overall rate is higher because $90\%$ of B's patients were in good condition compared with $60\%$ of A's. Choose Hospital A.
solution:
(a) Hospital A: $\frac{590 + 300}{1000} = \frac{890}{1000} = 89\%$.

Hospital B: $\frac{870 + 70}{1000} = \frac{940}{1000} = 94\%$.

(b) Good condition: A $\frac{590}{600} = 98.3\%$; B $\frac{870}{900} = 96.7\%$.

Poor condition: A $\frac{300}{400} = 75\%$; B $\frac{70}{100} = 70\%$.

(c) Hospital A has the higher survival rate for **both** groups of patients, yet Hospital B has the higher overall rate. This happens because the hospitals treat very different mixes of patients:

• Hospital A: $\frac{400}{1000} = 40\%$ of patients were in poor condition.
• Hospital B: $\frac{100}{1000} = 10\%$ of patients were in poor condition.

Patients in poor condition are much less likely to survive anywhere, and Hospital A treats far more of them, which drags its overall rate down. The overall figures mix together groups of very different sizes, so they are misleading here; the third variable (patient condition) reverses the comparison. This is called Simpson's paradox.

For a patient in poor condition, compare like with like: $75\% > 70\%$, so choose **Hospital A** (it is also better for patients in good condition).

question:
A researcher selected a random sample of 500 adults. Each adult was asked whether they usually use a phone or tablet in the hour before going to sleep, and how many hours they usually sleep per night.

| | Less than 6 h | 6 to 8 h | More than 8 h | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Screen use | 84 | 168 | 48 | 300 |
| No screen use | 26 | 124 | 50 | 200 |
| Total | 110 | 292 | 98 | 500 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the conditional distribution (as percentages) of sleep time for the adults who use a screen, and for the adults who do not.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Based on your answer to (a), does there appear to be an association between screen use and sleep time for adults? Justify your answer.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: If there were no association between screen use and sleep time, how many of the 300 screen users would you expect to sleep less than 6 hours? Show the work that leads to your answer, and compare it with the observed count.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A newspaper reports this study with the headline "Screens before bed cause shorter sleep". Is this conclusion justified? Explain.

hint: For (a) divide each count by its row total. For (c), with no association the screen users would have the same distribution as the whole sample.
answer: (a) Screen use: $28\%$, $56\%$, $16\%$; no screen use: $13\%$, $62\%$, $25\%$ (b) Yes: screen users are more likely to sleep less than 6 h ($28\%$ vs $13\%$) and less likely to sleep more than 8 h ($16\%$ vs $25\%$). (c) $300 \times \frac{110}{500} = 66$; observed 84 is well above 66. (d) No: it is an observational study, so it cannot show cause and effect.
solution:
(a) Screen use (total 300): $\frac{84}{300} = 28\%$, $\frac{168}{300} = 56\%$, $\frac{48}{300} = 16\%$.

No screen use (total 200): $\frac{26}{200} = 13\%$, $\frac{124}{200} = 62\%$, $\frac{50}{200} = 25\%$.

1 pt: correct method (dividing by row totals); 1 pt: all six percentages correct.

(b) Yes. The conditional distributions differ clearly: $28\%$ of screen users sleep less than 6 hours compared with $13\%$ of non-users, and only $16\%$ of screen users sleep more than 8 hours compared with $25\%$ of non-users. Comparing raw counts (84 vs 26) would not be fair because the groups have different sizes. 1 pt for a comparison of conditional percentages in context.

(c) Overall, $\frac{110}{500} = 22\%$ of adults sleep less than 6 hours. With no association, $22\%$ of the screen users would too:
$$\text{expected} = 300 \times \frac{110}{500} = 66$$
1 pt for the method (row total $\times$ column total $\div$ grand total).

The observed count, 84, is 18 more than the 66 expected under no association, which supports the association described in (b). 1 pt for the answer and the comparison.

(d) No. This is an observational study: the adults chose whether to use screens. Other variables (such as stress, shift work or caffeine use) could be linked to both screen use and short sleep, so the study can show an association but not that screens **cause** shorter sleep. A randomised experiment would be needed. 1 pt.

question:
A general $2 \times 2$ two-way table has entries $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ (all positive):

| | Glasses | No glasses |
|---|---|---|
| Left-handed | $a$ | $b$ |
| Right-handed | $c$ | $d$ |

(a) Prove that the proportion of glasses-wearers who are left-handed equals the proportion of non-glasses-wearers who are left-handed if and only if $ad = bc$.

(b) In one class the table is

| | Glasses | No glasses |
|---|---|---|
| Left-handed | $x$ | 6 |
| Right-handed | $x + 4$ | $3x$ |

There is no association between handedness and wearing glasses. Find $x$ and the number of students in the class.

(c) For the class in (b), show that the proportion of left-handers who wear glasses equals the proportion of right-handers who wear glasses, and explain why part (a) means this had to happen.
hint: For (a), write both proportions as fractions, set them equal and cross-multiply. For (b), use $ad = bc$ to form a quadratic.
answer: (a) $\frac{a}{a+c} = \frac{b}{b+d} \iff a(b+d) = b(a+c) \iff ad = bc$ (b) $x = 4$; 30 students (c) $\frac{4}{10} = \frac{8}{20} = 0.4$; the condition $ad = bc$ is symmetric, so it also gives equal row proportions.
solution:
(a) Proportion of glasses-wearers who are left-handed $= \frac{a}{a + c}$; proportion of non-glasses-wearers who are left-handed $= \frac{b}{b + d}$. Since all denominators are positive,
$$\frac{a}{a + c} = \frac{b}{b + d} \iff a(b + d) = b(a + c) \iff ab + ad = ab + bc \iff ad = bc$$
Every step is reversible, so the result holds in both directions.

(b) No association, so $ad = bc$:
$$x \cdot 3x = 6(x + 4)$$
$$3x^2 - 6x - 24 = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0 \Rightarrow (x - 4)(x + 2) = 0$$
$x = 4$ or $x = -2$; a count cannot be negative, so $x = 4$.

Table: left-handed 4 and 6; right-handed 8 and 12. Total $= 4 + 6 + 8 + 12 = 30$ students.

Check: $\frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{6}{18} = \frac{1}{3}$ ✓

(c) Left-handers who wear glasses: $\frac{4}{4 + 6} = 0.4$; right-handers who wear glasses: $\frac{8}{8 + 12} = 0.4$. Equal ✓

Repeating the proof in (a) with rows and columns swapped, $\frac{a}{a+b} = \frac{c}{c+d} \iff a(c+d) = c(a+b) \iff ad = bc$. It is the **same** condition, so whenever the column proportions are equal the row proportions must be equal too: "no association" does not depend on which variable you condition on.
